items.title: IPCC AR6 on attribution
items.claim: IPCC AR6 Working Group I (2021) concluded what about the cause of observed warming since around 1850?

options.text: It is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land

items.reveal:
The AR6 WGI Summary for Policymakers (2021) used 'unequivocal' for the first time in IPCC headline statements.

The assessment also tightened estimates of climate sensitivity to a likely range of 2.5-4 C per CO2 doubling.
items.why: IPCC's calibrated language tracks evolving confidence as evidence accumulates.

items.title: Solar cost decline
items.claim: Utility-scale solar PV levelised cost of electricity (LCOE) fell by roughly how much between 2010 and 2022?
items.reveal:
IRENA's 2023 cost report found utility-scale solar PV LCOE fell from around $0.45/kWh in 2010 to $0.049/kWh in 2022 in real terms.

Wind and battery costs followed similar trajectories.
items.why: Technology learning curves can outpace policy timelines on energy transition.

items.title: Amazon dieback risk
items.claim: Research from the early 2020s suggests parts of the Amazon may be approaching a tipping point at what threshold of deforestation?
items.reveal:
Lovejoy and Nobre (2018) proposed a tipping point of 20-25% deforestation, combined with climate change, beyond which large parts of the Amazon could shift to savanna.

Deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon stood near 17% by 2020 by INPE measurements.
items.why: Ecosystem tipping points have policy salience even when their exact value is uncertain.
